intent.raw_query: Montreal food and festivals, $1500 solo, 4 days, July 2027, from Toronto

experiences.name: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, and local charcuterie. Chat with vendors and discover the heart of Montreal's food culture in a vibrant, authentic setting.

trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Use this time to travel from the airport to your Old Montreal accommodation. Take the 747 express bus to downtown for ~$11 CAD, then connect via metro or walk to Old Montreal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Orientation Walk & Food Crawl: After checking in, explore the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal on foot. Stop at Schwartz's Deli for a classic Montreal smoked meat sandwich (~$12 CAD), stroll along Rue Saint-Paul, peek into Notre-Dame Basilica from outside (free exterior), and wander through Place Jacques-Cartier to soak up the lively street atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head toward the Quartier des Spectacles to catch free Montreal Jazz Festival street performances. The festival runs nightly with multiple free outdoor stages — grab a cold drink from a nearby dépanneur (corner store) and enjoy world-class jazz under the summer sky at no cost.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a convenience snack on arrival (~$8–10 CAD)
meals.dinner: Marché de la Villette (Old Montreal) — rustic French-Canadian bistro with affordable charcuterie boards and sandwiches (~$15–18 CAD). Alternatively, pick up fresh bread, cheese, and cold cuts from a nearby dépanneur for a budget picnic near the waterfront (~$10 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: The 747 airport bus is the most budget-friendly airport transfer. Pick up an OPUS card ($6 CAD) at the airport and load a day pass or single fares. The Jazz Festival typically runs late June through early July — confirm exact 2027 dates, as the free outdoor performances are the highlight and worth planning around.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon station. Spend the morning exploring one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample Quebec cheeses, taste maple products, pick up fresh seasonal fruits, and chat with local vendors. Budget ~$15–20 CAD for tastings and small purchases. This is the best way to experience authentic Québécois food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood and explore Avenue du Mont-Royal. Browse vintage and thrift shops (great for budget souvenirs), grab a coffee at a local café, and stroll through Parc Lafontaine — a gorgeous free green space with a lake, ideal for a relaxing picnic with market finds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for another evening of free Montreal Jazz Festival performances. Different artists and genres perform each night across multiple free outdoor stages. Arrive early to claim a good spot and enjoy the electric summer atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh croissant and coffee from a boulangerie near Old Montreal (~$5–7 CAD). Try Olive + Gourmando on Rue Saint-Paul for affordable morning pastries.
meals.lunch: Eat at Jean-Talon Market itself — grab a fresh baguette, local cheese, and seasonal produce directly from vendors for a self-assembled picnic lunch (~$10–12 CAD).
meals.dinner: Au Pied de Cochon is iconic but pricey — instead, try La Banquise on Rue Rachel for world-famous poutine, open 24/7 with portions starting at ~$12 CAD. A true Montreal must-eat on a budget.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is free to enter. Bring a small reusable bag for purchases. The metro ride from Old Montreal (Champ-de-Mars or Place-d'Armes station) to Jean-Talon is about 25 minutes and costs ~$3.75 CAD each way with an OPUS card.

day_by_day.morning: Mont Royal Park Hike: Start the day with a free morning hike up Mont Royal — Montreal's iconic hill and green lung. The walk from the base to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout takes about 30–40 minutes and offers stunning panoramic views of the city skyline. Pack a light snack from a nearby dépanneur before heading up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End Neighbourhood Exploration: Head to the trendy Mile End district. Walk along Boulevard Saint-Laurent and Rue Bernard. Visit Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel (both legendary, ~$1.50–2 CAD per bagel fresh from the oven) — a quintessential Montreal experience. Browse street art, murals, and independent boutiques without spending a dime.
day_by_day.evening: Jazz Festival Final Night: Head back to the Quartier des Spectacles for the free outdoor performances. Friday nights typically feature bigger headliner acts on the outdoor stages. The area buzzes with locals and tourists alike — enjoy a BYOB picnic on the festival grounds (outdoor public drinking is permitted in designated festival zones) with snacks from a dépanneur to keep costs low.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at the accommodation using market finds from Day 2, or grab a coffee and muffin from a local café (~$5 CAD).
meals.lunch: Fresh Montreal bagels from Fairmount or St-Viateur with cream cheese (~$4–6 CAD total) eaten as a casual street lunch in Mile End.
meals.dinner: Wilensky's Light Lunch (Mile End) — a historic Montreal institution serving the famous 'Special' grilled salami and bologna sandwich for under $6 CAD. Cash only, no substitutions — an authentic and ultra-budget Montreal meal.

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal Park is entirely free. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The hike is moderate and suitable for most fitness levels. Mile End is easily walkable from the Laurier or Mont-Royal metro stations. Check the Jazz Festival schedule online in advance to plan which free stages to prioritize on Friday night.

day_by_day.morning: Old Port & Waterfront Stroll: Spend a leisurely last morning along the Old Port waterfront (Vieux-Port). Walk the promenade along the St. Lawrence River, watch street performers, and admire the historic architecture. The Bonsecours Market building is free to walk around and photograph. Soak in the charm of Old Montreal one last time before checking out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Piknic Électronik at Parc Jean-Drapeau (Note: Piknic runs Sundays — if your schedule allows extending to Sunday July 18 or adjusting, prioritize this. If Saturday is your last full day, substitute with a visit to Parc Jean-Drapeau via the free Jacques-Cartier Bridge walk or Île Sainte-Hélène metro stop for a free afternoon in nature, with views of the city and the Biosphère exterior).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal: End your trip with a celebratory but budget-friendly dinner. Try L'Gros Luxe on Rue Ontario for creative comfort food and cocktails with a festive atmosphere (~$18–22 CAD per person). Afterward, take a final evening walk through the illuminated cobblestone streets of Old Montreal and along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico in Mile End (if passing through) or a local Old Montreal café — café au lait and a croissant (~$6–8 CAD).
meals.lunch: Marché Bonsecours area food trucks or grab a falafel wrap from a street vendor near Place Jacques-Cartier (~$8–10 CAD).
meals.dinner: L'Gros Luxe or Resto Plateau (Rue Saint-Denis) for hearty Québécois comfort food. Budget ~$18–22 CAD per person including a local Boréale craft beer.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is on July 19 or later, strongly consider adjusting Day 4 to a Sunday to include Piknic Électronik at Parc Jean-Drapeau — it runs every Sunday from May to October and is one of Montreal's most beloved outdoor events with a modest entrance fee (~$20–25 CAD). It would pair perfectly with the festival theme of this trip. Pack sunscreen for all outdoor days — 25°C summer weather means strong UV exposure.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Travel to Old Montreal Stay hotel, check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Food Crawl: After settling in, explore the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal on foot. Stop at Schwartz's Deli for iconic smoked meat, browse the historic Marché Bonsecours area, and sample local treats from nearby delis and patisseries. The hotel's central location makes this a perfect first afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances: Head to the Quartier des Spectacles (a short walk or quick metro ride from Old Montreal) to catch free outdoor Jazz Festival performances. Soak in the vibrant summer atmosphere, street musicians, and festive crowds under the warm July evening sky.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Schwartz's Deli on Boulevard Saint-Laurent — try the classic smoked meat sandwich with coleslaw and a pickle (~$18–22 CAD per person).
meals.dinner: Garde Manger in Old Montreal — a beloved mid-range bistro known for creative Quebec cuisine. Budget ~$45–60 CAD per person with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light on logistics. The Jazz Festival typically runs late June through early July, but check the exact 2027 dates — if it overlaps with July 15, this is a must. Pack comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Spend the morning sampling Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, artisan breads, seasonal fruits, and local charcuterie from vendor stalls. Arrive early (~9:30–10:00) for the best selection and atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End Bagel and Brunch Experience: From Jean-Talon, walk or take a short bus ride to the bohemian Mile End neighborhood. Visit both the legendary St-Viateur Bagel Shop and Fairmount Bagel — taste and compare Montreal's iconic wood-fired bagels. Stroll Rue Bernard and Avenue Laurier to browse indie boutiques and soak up the neighborhood's creative vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for more Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances. Enjoy the free outdoor stages, grab a local craft beer from a festival vendor, and experience the electric energy of one of the world's greatest music festivals.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a café in Old Montreal before heading to Jean-Talon.
meals.lunch: Graze at Jean-Talon Market stalls — assemble a picnic-style meal with local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and seasonal produce (~$15–20 CAD). Add a fresh-squeezed juice or maple lemonade.
meals.dinner: L'Express on Rue Saint-Denis — a classic Montreal French bistro with a lively atmosphere. Try the steak tartare or duck confit. Budget ~$40–55 CAD per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a reusable bag to Jean-Talon Market — it's easy to pick up edible souvenirs like maple syrup, local honey, or artisan jams. Mile End is best explored on foot; the two bagel shops are about a 10-minute walk apart.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic heart of Old Montreal at a relaxed pace. Visit the stunning Notre-Dame Basilica (book tickets in advance, ~$15 CAD), stroll along the Old Port waterfront, and browse the artisan vendors along Rue Saint-Paul. Enjoy the warm morning weather along the St. Lawrence River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Piknic Électronik at Parc Jean-Drapeau: Note — Piknic Électronik runs on Sundays, so today enjoy a relaxed afternoon exploring Parc Jean-Drapeau independently. Take the metro to Île Sainte-Hélène, walk the grounds, visit the iconic Biosphère environmental museum (~$22 CAD), and enjoy views of the river and city skyline. Save Piknic for Sunday (Day 4).
day_by_day.evening: Plateau-Mont-Royal neighborhood exploration. Take the metro to the Plateau and wander Rue Mont-Royal and Avenue du Parc. Browse local boutiques, street art, and lively terrasses (outdoor patios). This is one of Montreal's most vibrant and characterful neighborhoods, perfect for a Friday evening.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico in Mile End (if passing through) or a neighborhood café near the hotel — known for excellent espresso and a local crowd (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.lunch: Crew Collective & Café or a terrace spot in Old Montreal — try a Quebec-style poutine or a fresh sandwich (~$18–25 CAD).
meals.dinner: Au Pied de Cochon (if budget allows, slightly upscale) or Joe Beef's neighborhood rival Liverpool House on Rue Notre-Dame Ouest — hearty Quebec cuisine with a festive Friday atmosphere. Budget ~$55–75 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Notre-Dame Basilica is extremely popular in summer — pre-book your entry ticket online. The Biosphère is a great rainy-day backup if there's any precipitation. Friday evenings in the Plateau are especially lively with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Old Port area for a morning kayak or paddleboat rental along the St. Lawrence waterfront (available from the Old Port marina, ~$20–30 CAD/hour). Alternatively, rent a BIXI bike (Montreal's public bike-share, ~$7/day) and cycle the scenic waterfront path toward Habitat 67 for great photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Piknic Électronik at Parc Jean-Drapeau: Note — Piknic runs on Sundays; if your trip extends to Sunday July 19, this is the highlight. For Saturday afternoon, explore the vibrant Atwater Market near the Lachine Canal — smaller than Jean-Talon but beloved by locals for artisan food stalls, local wine, and a relaxed atmosphere. Cycle or walk the Lachine Canal path.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening celebration back in Old Montreal. Take a guided evening walk through the illuminated cobblestone streets, enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop or terrace restaurant, and end the night with a Quebec craft cocktail or local microbrewery beer at a bar on Rue Saint-Paul or Place Jacques-Cartier.

meals.breakfast: Olive + Gourmando in Old Montreal — beloved local café with exceptional pastries, avocado toast, and house-made granola. Expect a short wait on weekends (~$16–22 CAD).
meals.lunch: Atwater Market picnic — pick up artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh baguette, and local cider for a picnic along the Lachine Canal (~$20–25 CAD assembled).
meals.dinner: Maggie Oakes or Brasserie 701 in Old Montreal — upscale-casual farewell dinner with locally sourced Quebec ingredients and a great wine list. Budget ~$50–65 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight or checkout allows, Sunday July 19 is ideal for Piknic Électronik at Parc Jean-Drapeau (starts around 14:00, entry ~$20–25 CAD) — the perfect Montreal send-off. BIXI bikes are a fantastic and affordable way to see the city; the app makes renting easy. Keep an umbrella handy given the 30mm monthly rain average, though July showers are typically brief.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Montreal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer by private car service to Old Montreal Stay hotel. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal to get your bearings. Admire the stunning architecture of Notre-Dame Basilica and the Vieux-Port waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Food Crawl: Begin your Montreal culinary adventure with a guided food crawl through the historic cobblestone streets of Old Montreal. Stop at iconic spots including Schwartz's Deli for legendary smoked meat, local fromageries for Quebec artisan cheeses, and specialty shops for poutine and other regional delicacies. This immersive introduction to Montreal's food culture is perfectly situated near your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Place des Arts area to catch the Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances. Experience world-class free outdoor jazz concerts in a vibrant festival atmosphere as the sun sets over the city. The warm summer evening (around 20–22°C) makes this an ideal open-air experience.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a welcome amenity or light snack at the hotel upon arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled given the midday arrival.
meals.lunch: Tasting stops during the Old Montreal Food Crawl serve as a satisfying early afternoon meal — smoked meat, cheeses, and local bites at iconic spots along the route.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's legendary fine-dining institution by chef Normand Laprise. Located steps from Old Montreal, Toqué! offers a stunning tasting menu showcasing the finest Quebec seasonal ingredients. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairings for a true luxury welcome dinner. (Expect CAD $200–$300 per person with pairings.)

day_by_day.notes: Book private airport transfer in advance. Confirm Old Montreal Food Crawl booking ahead of time. Toqué! reservations are essential and should be made weeks in advance — book the earliest available dinner seating around 18:30 to allow time after the food crawl. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel and Brunch Experience: Take a private car or scenic 20-minute ride to the bohemian Mile End neighborhood. Visit both legendary bagel institutions — St-Viateur Bagel Shop and Fairmount Bagel — to taste freshly wood-fired Montreal bagels hot from the oven. Explore the vibrant street art and boutique culture of this iconic neighborhood. A curated brunch stop at a top Mile End café rounds out the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Journey to one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. A premium guided tour leads you through stalls brimming with Quebec cheeses, maple products, heirloom vegetables, artisan charcuterie, and fresh summer fruits. Meet local producers, sample generously, and pick up artisan souvenirs. The market is in full summer glory in July with peak produce on display.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Montreal area and enjoy a sunset cocktail on a rooftop terrace overlooking the St. Lawrence River. Then head back to the Jazz Festival at Place des Arts for an evening headliner concert — July is peak festival season and world-renowned artists perform nightly on the main outdoor stages.

meals.breakfast: Fresh wood-fired bagels with house-made cream cheese and smoked salmon at St-Viateur or Fairmount Bagel — the quintessential Montreal morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Damas Restaurant in Mile End or Plateau — an acclaimed Syrian-Mediterranean fine-dining gem near the bagel and market circuit. Enjoy a luxurious mezze spread with premium Lebanese wines. (CAD $80–$120 per person.)
meals.dinner: Le Serpent — a sleek, upscale Italian-influenced restaurant in Old Montreal set inside a stunning converted industrial space. Known for handmade pastas, exceptional seafood, and a world-class natural wine list. Perfect for a sophisticated dinner after the Jazz Festival performances. (CAD $100–$160 per person with wine.)

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is most vibrant in the morning and early afternoon — the guided tour timing aligns perfectly after the bagel experience. Wear light, breathable clothing for the warm 25°C afternoon. Bring a small tote bag for market purchases. Check the Jazz Festival schedule in advance to identify must-see evening performers and arrive early for prime viewing spots.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a leisurely luxury breakfast at the hotel, then embark on a private guided walking tour of Old Montreal's historic architecture and art galleries. Explore the Pointe-à-Callière Museum — Montreal's archaeology and history museum built on the city's actual founding site — for a premium behind-the-scenes cultural experience. The cool indoor galleries are a welcome respite if the afternoon heats up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to Île Sainte-Hélène via the scenic metro or private water taxi to experience Piknic Électronik at Parc Jean-Drapeau. This beloved weekly outdoor electronic music festival runs every Sunday — however, on Fridays in July, special festival-season editions are sometimes scheduled. If the Friday edition is not available, enjoy a private guided kayak or paddleboard experience along the St. Lawrence waterfront near the Old Port, followed by a relaxing afternoon at a luxury spa (Bota Bota Spa-sur-l'eau, a floating spa on a converted ferry in the Old Port, is an exceptional premium option).
day_by_day.evening: Jazz Festival Grand Evening: This is peak Jazz Festival weekend. Dress up for a premium ticketed indoor concert at Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier or Théâtre Maisonneuve at Place des Arts, featuring world-class headline artists. Follow with a nightcap at a sophisticated jazz bar in the Quartier des Spectacles.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury breakfast at the hotel — freshly baked viennoiseries, Quebec yogurt with local honey, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed juices served in an elegant setting.
meals.lunch: Garde Manger — celebrity chef Chuck Hughes' legendary Old Montreal seafood brasserie. Indulge in a premium seafood plateau with lobster, oysters, and crab claws alongside craft cocktails. (CAD $100–$150 per person.) Perfect pre-afternoon activity fuel.
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — Daniel Boulud's acclaimed Montreal outpost offering refined French cuisine with Quebec terroir influences in one of the city's most opulent dining rooms. The summer tasting menu with wine pairings is exceptional. (CAD $200–$350 per person with pairings.) Reserve the private dining room for an ultra-exclusive experience.

day_by_day.notes: Verify the Piknic Électronik Friday schedule for July 2027 closer to the trip date — the Sunday format is guaranteed but special Friday editions vary by year. Bota Bota Spa-sur-l'eau requires advance reservations and is highly recommended as an alternative or add-on. Maison Boulud at the Ritz must be booked well in advance. Smart-casual to formal attire recommended for the evening concert and dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, indulgent final morning in Montreal. Enjoy a premium brunch at a celebrated Old Montreal or Plateau restaurant. Take a final stroll through the Vieux-Port waterfront market, picking up last-minute artisan gifts — Quebec maple products, local jams, artisan chocolates, and ice ciders make perfect luxury souvenirs. Visit a high-end Quebec design boutique for a unique keepsake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Parc Jean-Drapeau for the Sunday-style Piknic Électronik experience (note: if departure allows, the Sunday edition on July 19 is the guaranteed weekly event — consider adjusting checkout to catch it). Alternatively, enjoy a private guided bike tour along the scenic Canal de Lachine, passing through the vibrant Saint-Henri and Verdun neighborhoods with stops at artisan coffee roasters and local chocolatiers.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Montreal's most celebrated addresses before any late departures or a final evening in the city. Explore the lively Quartier Latin or Plateau for a final taste of Montreal's legendary nightlife and live music scene.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Olive + Gourmando in Old Montreal — a beloved artisan café famous for its exceptional house-baked breads, premium sandwiches, and inventive brunch plates. Arrive early as lines form quickly, or opt for a private reservation if available. (CAD $30–$50 per person.)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch assembled from Old Port market finds — premium charcuterie, aged Quebec cheeses, fresh baguette, and local strawberries enjoyed riverside at the Vieux-Port with a chilled bottle of Quebec ice cider.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Jun I — Montreal's premier Japanese fine-dining experience by chef Jun Morita, offering an exquisite omakase or kaiseki tasting menu that showcases the finest local Quebec ingredients through a Japanese culinary lens. An unforgettable, unique finale to a premium Montreal journey. (CAD $150–$250 per person with sake or wine pairings.)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange a private luxury transfer for departure. If the trip extends to Sunday July 19, the guaranteed weekly Piknic Électronik at Parc Jean-Drapeau (14:00–21:00) is a perfect final afternoon activity. Jun I reservations are highly sought after — book as early as possible. Pack artisan market purchases carefully; Quebec maple products and local preserves are TSA/CATSA compliant in checked luggage.
